options.fullText:
- Take requests as stated
  - Don't infer what the user "really meant"
  - Don't add to it
  - Don't change it
- Applies whenever you turn their words into
  - Tasks
  - Specs
  - Rules
  - Instructions for others
- Why: an agent got it wrong twice
  - Mistake 1
    - User: "be brief"
    - Agent: "keep it to one line"
    - User never limited length
    - Agent added a limit itself
  - Mistake 2
    - User: "never add details I didn't state"
    - Agent: "record in the user's own words"
    - User never forbade rewording
      - Only adding or changing detail
      - Less constraining than exact words
  - Same mistake both times
    - A gap
    - Filled with the agent's own guess
    - Presented as the user's words
- Agents infer and guess far too much
- Never add what wasn't stated
  - No detail
  - No limit
  - No number
  - No rule
- A gap in the request?
  - Name it as your assumption
  - Ask, or leave it open
  - Never quietly make it a rule

- Read requests sensibly
- Small gaps
  - Fill them with reasonable choices
- List every assumption
  - At the end

- Interpret requests freely
  - Infer what the user most likely wants
  - Decide gaps yourself

- Before starting, ask or confirm with the user
  - Never assume any of these
- What it's for
  - The goal
  - Who it's for: the target audience or users
- Stage of the work, for example
  - Tech spike
  - Prototype
  - Class project
  - Alpha
  - Beta
  - Production
- Scale
  - How many users, how much data, how long it must last
- Technology
  - Language
  - Stack and frameworks
  - Where it runs or deploys
- Constraints
  - Deadline
  - Budget, including paid services
  - Anything it must work with
- What done looks like
- These are examples, not the full list
  - Ask about anything else the work depends on

- Ask only about what's unclear
  - Goal, audience, stage, scale, technology, constraints, what done looks like
- State what you assumed for the rest

- Don't ask
- Use sensible defaults
  - State them at the start

- True = only what you were given
- Other files or work
  - Only when told you may
  - Only as told

- True only when confirmed
  - By current official sources
    - Documentation
    - Specifications
    - Release notes
    - Issue tracker
  - Or by running it yourself
- Training memory = hypothesis
  - Until checked
- Cite each fact's source

- Use anything that helps
  - In the project
  - In the environment

- Never reinvent a wheel
- Prioritize
  - Industry standards
  - Proven patterns
  - How major products and libraries already do it
- Find them with good, broad research
  - Generic search terms
  - NOT searches built on your own guesses
- Your own reasoning is no substitute
- Departing from the standard pattern
  - Approval first
  - Say what the pattern is
  - Say why you depart

- Before writing general-purpose code
  - Check for a maintained library
- Build what's needed directly

- Exactly what was asked
  - No more
  - No less
- Nothing outside the scope
  - Not added
  - Not cleaned up
  - Not "improved"
  - However tempting
- Noticed something outside it?
  - Report it
  - Don't act on it
- Can't build a piece to spec?
  - Leave it incomplete
  - Never substitute

- Stay in scope
- Small related fixes OK
  - List each one

- Can't build it as specified?
  - Build the closest working version
  - Say what differs

- An escalation is a blocker
  - Post it
  - Stop
  - Do NOT pick
- Blocked means
  - Instruction silent on your decision
  - Tests contradict each other
  - Test contradicts the instruction
  - Piece can't be built to spec
  - You need something not given
- One question per escalation
  - Question
  - Context (file:line)
  - Options
  - Blocking: yes
- Not blocking? Not an escalation
  - Decide yourself
  - Record it in your response

options.shortName: Handle it only if in scope
options.fullText:
- Blocked?
  - Fix it yourself only within strict scope
  - Otherwise stop and ask

- Unsure?
  - Decide
  - Keep going
- List your decisions
  - At the end
- Unsure? Ask

- Don't alternate asking and working
- Research first
- Then ask all questions together
  - One at a time
- Answers raise new questions?
  - Research again
  - Then ask the new ones together
- Ask questions as they come up

- A choice? Make it yourself
- Say what you chose

- A choice? List the options you see
  - Briefly
- Say which you'd pick

- A choice? Research it first
- Then present
  - The options
  - What you found
  - Your recommendation
- Asking is not researching

- A choice? Research it first
- Then present
  - The options
  - Their trade-offs
- Recommend none

- Big picture first
  - "If we can't solve the big picture first, how can we hope to build the details?"
- Every part hollow before full
  - Exists
  - Reachable
  - Testable from outside
  - Returns a placeholder
- Decided in the hollow stage
  - Interfaces
  - Types
  - Names
- Unknown content?
  - The part still exists
  - It says what to find out
- Interface tests first
  - Pass against placeholders
- Filling adds no new structure
  - Missing structure found later?
  - Design change
  - Back to the user

- One thin slice end to end
- Then extend it
- Build in whatever order makes sense

- Break work into sprint features
- Each feature
  - Strictly defined interface
  - A standalone tool
  - Own definition of done
  - Own integration tests
  - Delivered with
    - README
    - Packaging
    - Example code

- Break work into small tasks
  - Each done in one sitting
- Do the work as one piece

- Object-oriented
  - Small single-purpose classes
  - Composition over inheritance

- Functional
  - Pure functions
  - No mutation
  - Side effects at the edges
- Use the codebase's existing patterns

- Separable piece = standalone module
- Knows nothing of its user
  - No project names
  - No project assumptions
  - No reaching into caller data
- Liftable into any project
  - Small, explicit interface
  - Own short docs
  - Own tests
- Project glue
  - Thin
  - Separate from the modules

- Split work into parts
  - Small, explicit interfaces
- Abstract only on a second use

- Name for what it IS or DOES
- NEVER for implementation
  - `retry_with_backoff`, not `loop_helper`
  - `customer_lookup`, not `redis_cache_wrapper`
- NEVER for who uses it
  - Applies a rule to a string?
  - It's a `string_rule_applier`
  - Even if only checkout calls it
- Paper and pencil analogy
  - You map with them
  - They aren't a "mapper tool"
  - They're writing and recording tools
- Clear outside any app context
  - No app or product branding
- Err toward verbose
  - A sentence-long name beats a vague one

- Short, idiomatic names
  - In the language's style
  - In the framework's style
- Name things like the codebase does

- Specify every format
- What you build
  - Whitespace
  - Alignment
  - Line endings
  - Headers
  - Error messages
- Work products
  - File layout
  - Naming
  - Commit shape
- Documentation
  - README sections
  - Report structure
- Undecided format?
  - Name it as discretion
  - Never silent
- Format like the project already does
- Formatting is your call
- No tests

- Test what you've made
  - Ensure it works

- Test first
  - Interface level
  - Module level
- Automated tests
  - Wherever possible
  - In git or similar
  - Alongside the code
- Each module
  - Interface tests first
  - They fail
  - Then pass once built
- Finer tests inside modules
  - Your discretion
- Integration tests fully real
  - Real entry points
  - Real services
  - Real data
- Unit tests pass?
  - Time to integration test
  - NOT done yet

- Strict test-first TDD
  - Every behaviour
- Automated tests
  - In version control

options.shortName: Research errors, never guess and retry
options.fullText:
- No "try and repeat" loops
  - Skipping proper research
  - Testing random guesses
  - In slow, expensive workflows
- The cost
  - Hours wasted
  - Hundreds of dollars
- NOT authorized
  - Wild guesses through CI/CD
- Errors MUST be researched
  - Good generic search terms
  - NOT niche terms from your hypothesis
    - That's as bad as guessing

- Try quick, cheap experiments first
- Not settled?
  - Research

- Costs money per use?
  - Explicit permission first

- Costs money per use?
  - Research the fix first
  - Prove it first

- Costs money per use?
  - Research the fix
  - Prove it
  - Then ask permission

- Paid runs: your judgement
  - Within [time / usage / cost limit]
- No limits on paid runs
- No documentation

- Existing docs your change makes wrong
  - Update them

- A README for everything you build
  - What it is
  - How to use it
  - An example

- Document each part
  - README
  - Interface
  - Decisions made, and why

- Stacked PRs
  - Keep working, don't wait on merges
- Review each PR
  - By a separate agent
- One pull request at the end

- Commit directly
  - No pull requests
- Suggest work that can run in parallel
- One thing at a time

- No repository
  - Don't create one
  - Don't commit

- Local git repository only
  - Create one if there is none
  - Commit as you go
  - Never push to a remote

- Local git repository, pushed to a remote
  - Create them if there are none
    - Ask before creating the remote
  - Commit and push as you go

- Use the existing repository
  - Don't create a new one
  - Follow its branches and commit conventions

- End with
  - Status
  - Built
  - Tests: commands and results
  - Deviations
  - Decisions
  - Open items

- Respond wiki style
  - Headings
  - Short indented bullets
  - No prose paragraphs

- Respond like slides
  - Short titled sections
  - 3–5 bullets each

- Start with a TL;DR
  - One or two sentences
- Give only the answer or result

- Condensed
  - Nested fragments
  - No filler
  - No lost facts
  - Outcome first, detail nested under it
  - Every list split into bullets
  - A contrast stays on one line
- Example
  - Before
    - "I bumped the S3 retry count from 3 to 5 on the platform team's suggestion, though I doubt it fixes the timeouts since the failures we saw were permission errors rather than load. I did not touch the parquet writer, which is still the slowest step."
  - Not quite
    ```
    - S3 retry count 3 -> 5
      - Platform team's suggestion
      - Doubt it fixes the timeouts
      - Failures
        - Permission errors
      - Success
        - Load
    - Parquet writer NOT touched
      - Still the slowest step
    ```
  - Why not quite
    - "Success: load" was never said
      - Splitting the contrast invented it
    - The reason sits beside the doubt, not under it
    - "I" dropped
      - "NOT touched" now claims no one touched it
  - Ideal
    ```
    - I bumped the S3 retry count 3 -> 5
      - Platform team's suggestion
      - I doubt it fixes the timeouts
        - Failures we saw were permission errors, not load
    - I did NOT touch the parquet writer
      - Still the slowest step
    ```

- Research only
  - Change nothing
- Use official sources
  - Cite every finding
- Keep apart
  - Established
  - Likely
  - Unknown

- Research the realistic options
- Compare side by side
  - With sources
- Don't choose
  - Unless asked

- Find the answer
  - Reliable source
  - Cite it
- Then stop

- Prove one thing works
  - Before real work depends on it
- Keep it minimal
  - Smallest possible
  - Fastest possible
  - Throwaway code
    - Never the start of the real build
- State the question first
- Show the proof
  - Commands and output
  - Or screenshots
- Can't judge it yourself?
  - Video, motion, feel
  - Say so
  - Ask for a human check
- End with
  - Answer: works / doesn't / partly
  - The proof
  - What the real build must know

- Prove it works
- Small, clean prototype
  - The real build grows from it

- Reproduce the bug first
  - Show the reproduction
- Find the cause
  - With evidence
  - Before changing anything
  - No guess-and-retry
- Fix the cause
  - Not the symptom
  - No workarounds
- Add a test
  - Fails without the fix
  - Passes with it
- Change nothing else

- Find the likely cause
- Fix it
- Show the problem is gone

- Review only
  - Change nothing
- Check every requirement
  - One by one
- Verify claims yourself
  - Read the code
  - Run the tests
  - Run the program
- Unverifiable claim = NOT met
- Each item
  - Met or NOT met
  - With evidence
- List defects
  - By severity
  - File and line

- Read the change
- Point out
  - Anything wrong
  - Anything risky
- Change nothing
